newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral to meet Sri Lankan foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral to meet Sri Lankan foreign minister.

text.p: Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar has arrived in the Indian capital to meet new prime minister Inder Kumar Gujral, diplomats said on Thursday.

Kadirgamar arrived in New Delhi late on Wednesday and was expected to see Gujral, who also holds the foreign and finance portfolios, on Friday, Sri Lanka's deputy high commissioner C.R. Jayasinghe said.
"It is a goodwill visit. He knows I.K. Gujral very well," Jayasinghe said.
Kadirgamar will be the first visiting foreign dignitary to meet Gujral, 77, since he took office on Monday at the head of a centre-left government.
Earlier this week Sri Lanka welcomed Gujral's appointment, calling him an old friend who will further strengthen ties between the two neighbours.

Indo-Sri Lanka relations touched a low in the late 1980s after Indian troops arrived in the island to disarm rebels of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) under a controversial agreement between the two countries.
But ties have improved dramatically since President Chandrika Kumaratunga's People's Alliance took power in 1994.
On Thursday, LTTE rebels said they hoped Gujral would support the self-determination rights of Tamils in the island's north and east.

The clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored in Vavuniya, 220 km (138 miles) north of Colombo, quoted an LTTE letter to Gujral as saying Tamils in Sri Lanka's northeast wanted to maintain a strategic and historical relationship with India.
